requirements.name: EIN (Employer Identification Number)
requirements.note: Needed for banking, hiring, and taxes

requirements.name: Employment eligibility verification
requirements.note: Required for every employee, completed within days of the start date

requirements.name: Packaged-food labeling rules
requirements.note: Only if selling packaged or bottled items

requirements.name: Business entity registration
requirements.note: Skip for sole proprietors, but check name registration rules

requirements.name: Sales tax / seller's permit
requirements.note: Required to collect tax on food sales

requirements.name: Food handler / manager certification
requirements.note: Handler card for staff, manager certificate for the person in charge

requirements.name: Workers' compensation insurance
requirements.note: Required once you have employees

requirements.name: Alcoholic beverage license
requirements.note: Long lead time, often restricted for mobile vendors

requirements.name: Vehicle registration and commercial insurance
requirements.agency: State motor vehicle agency and insurer (demo)
requirements.note: Commercial coverage, not personal

requirements.name: Mobile food facility health permit
requirements.note: Includes plan review and vehicle inspection

requirements.name: Commissary / base kitchen agreement
requirements.note: Home kitchens are generally not allowed for truck prep

requirements.name: Food-safety and temperature-control plan
requirements.note: Required for meat, dairy, eggs, cooked rice; simpler plan for other menus

requirements.name: City business license
requirements.note: Separate from state registration

requirements.name: Street vending / curbside approval
requirements.note: Location zones, time limits, and distance rules apply

requirements.name: Fire safety inspection
requirements.note: Extra checks if you use propane or a generator

requirements.name: Propane / generator safety approval
requirements.note: Cylinder limits, secured storage, extinguisher rules

requirements.name: Farmers market / event vendor application
requirements.note: Often needs proof of insurance and permits

requirements.name: Private lot permission and zoning check
requirements.agency: Property owner and city zoning office (demo)
requirements.note: Written permission required from the owner

requirements.name: Catering / special event permit
requirements.note: Rules differ from regular service

requirements.name: Additional-jurisdiction permit
requirements.note: Permits usually do not transfer between jurisdictions

requirements.name: Late-night operation approval
requirements.note: Noise, lighting, and hours restrictions

restrictions.rule: No vending within a set distance of a brick-and-mortar restaurant (demo: 300 ft)
restrictions.verify: Ask public works for the current distance rule and any exceptions

restrictions.rule: Prohibited near schools during school hours (demo: 500 ft)
restrictions.verify: Check the city's vending zone map

restrictions.rule: No vending in residential-only zoning districts
restrictions.verify: Confirm the zoning designation of every spot with the planning office

restrictions.rule: Maximum stay per curbside spot (demo: 4 hours), no return the same day
restrictions.verify: Ask about posted time limits and metered zones

restrictions.rule: Operating hours restricted (demo: 7 AM to 10 PM); later hours need extra approval
restrictions.verify: Ask the permits office about late-night exceptions

restrictions.rule: Must obey street-cleaning schedules, meters, and fire hydrant clearance
restrictions.verify: Check posted signs at each spot

restrictions.rule: Generator noise limit (demo: 65 dB at 50 ft); no loud amplified music
restrictions.verify: Choose a quiet-rated generator and ask about the local noise ordinance

restrictions.rule: Limits on sandwich boards, flags, and sidewalk signs
restrictions.verify: Ask what signage is allowed outside the truck footprint

restrictions.rule: Must return to the commissary on a set schedule (demo: daily) for cleaning, water, and waste
restrictions.verify: Get the commissary log requirements in writing

restrictions.rule: No wastewater or grease discharge on streets or storm drains
restrictions.verify: Confirm the approved disposal method and record-keeping

restrictions.rule: Hot food held above and cold food below required temperatures, with logs
restrictions.verify: Ask for the current temperature standards

restrictions.rule: Restricted menu items or preparation methods on trucks (demo: raw shellfish, home-canned goods)
restrictions.verify: Submit your full menu during plan review

restrictions.rule: Menu or equipment changes after approval may need re-review
restrictions.verify: Ask what changes trigger a new review

restrictions.rule: Alcohol sales limited by license type, hours, and location; often banned from mobile vending
restrictions.verify: Ask the state alcohol agency whether mobile sales are permitted at all

restrictions.rule: Minimum wage, breaks, and overtime rules apply, plus food-handler cards for all staff
restrictions.verify: Confirm requirements with the state labor agency

restrictions.rule: Sales tax must be collected and filed on schedule, with tips and service fees treated per state rules
restrictions.verify: Ask the tax agency about filing frequency

restrictions.rule: Vehicle weight, size, and commercial-license limits for truck operators
restrictions.verify: Check the truck's weight against the license class needed

restrictions.rule: Propane cylinder count, storage, and placement limits, with extinguisher and hood system requirements
restrictions.verify: Get the fire department's mobile vendor checklist

restrictions.rule: Organizer rules: exclusivity clauses, menu overlap limits, required insurance, revenue share
restrictions.verify: Read the vendor agreement before paying any fee

restrictions.rule: Written owner consent, plus lot capacity and parking-count limits
restrictions.verify: Keep signed permission on the truck

restrictions.rule: Rules differ across city and county lines, and enforcement may be stricter in some areas
restrictions.verify: Confirm each jurisdiction separately

restrictions.rule: Trash and recycling receptacles required within a set radius of the truck, plus litter cleanup
restrictions.verify: Ask what radius applies

restrictions.rule: Catering may require advance notice to the health department and food-safe transport
restrictions.verify: Ask how many days of notice are required

go_live_roadmap.note: Durations are demo estimates in calendar days. Steps that share a dependency can run in parallel. Real timelines depend on your city and how quickly you respond to agencies.

phases.name: 1. Plan and set up the business

steps.name: Finalize concept, menu, and where you will sell
steps.what_to_do: Write your menu, pick selling channels, and list equipment needs. Health review is based on your menu, so settle it early.
steps.tip: Keep the first menu small. Fewer items means simpler plan review.

steps.name: Get your EIN and choose a business structure
steps.what_to_do: Decide sole proprietor vs LLC vs partnership, register if needed, and get your EIN.
steps.tip: An LLC takes longer but separates personal and business liability.

steps.name: Open a business bank account and set up bookkeeping
steps.what_to_do: Open the account with your EIN and set up simple expense tracking. Keep every receipt from day one.
steps.tip: Permit and inspection fees are all deductible, so track them.

steps.name: Get your city business license and sales tax permit
steps.what_to_do: Apply for the city license and the state seller's permit. Both are needed before the health permit.
steps.tip: Apply for both the same day to save a week.

steps.name: Complete food handler and manager certification
steps.what_to_do: Take the approved course and exam. Every person working in the truck needs their card.
steps.tip: Book this early. It is quick and often needed to submit the health application.

steps.name: Sign your commissary agreement
steps.what_to_do: Choose a licensed commissary, tour it, and sign the agreement. You will need it for the health permit.
steps.tip: Ask about storage, parking, and water and waste hookups before signing.

steps.name: Buy or lease your truck
steps.what_to_do: Source a vehicle suitable for a mobile food facility. Check weight, size, and layout against local rules before paying.
steps.tip: Ask the health department for their vehicle checklist before you buy.

steps.name: Submit your menu and truck plan for health review
steps.what_to_do: Send the menu, equipment list, and layout plan. Fix any comments before build-out.
steps.tip: Reviewing plans before build-out avoids expensive rework.

steps.name: Get commercial insurance and register the vehicle
steps.what_to_do: Buy commercial vehicle and liability coverage, then register the truck as a commercial vehicle.
steps.tip: Markets and events ask for proof of insurance. Get the certificate as a PDF.

steps.name: Build out and install equipment
steps.what_to_do: Install sinks, refrigeration, cooking equipment, and fire suppression per the approved plan.
steps.tip: Take photos of every stage. Inspectors may ask for proof.

steps.name: Apply for the health permit and pass inspection
steps.what_to_do: Submit the application with your license, commissary agreement, and plan approval. Book the vehicle inspection.
steps.tip: Use the inspection prep checklist and do a dry run first.

steps.name: Pass the fire safety inspection
steps.what_to_do: Book the fire inspection. If you use propane or a generator, complete the extra safety approval too.
steps.tip: Have tagged extinguishers and secured cylinders ready on inspection day.

steps.name: Get selling-location approvals
steps.what_to_do: Apply for street vending approval, market or event applications, private lot permission, catering and late-night approvals, and any second-jurisdiction permits you need.
steps.tip: Markets fill seasons early, so apply as soon as your health permit is in hand.

steps.name: Apply for an alcohol license
steps.what_to_do: Start early. This is the longest lead-time item and may not be available for mobile vendors.
steps.tip: Ask the agency first whether mobile sales are allowed at all.

steps.name: Set up hiring and payroll
steps.what_to_do: Complete workers' comp, payroll registration, and eligibility verification before the first shift.
steps.tip: Every employee needs a food handler card before working.

steps.name: Set up POS, payments, pricing, and supplier accounts
steps.what_to_do: Choose a payment system, finalize prices using your ingredient costs, and open accounts with suppliers.
steps.tip: Price for a 3 to 3.5 times markup on ingredients as a starting point.

steps.name: Brand the truck and set up social and map listings
steps.what_to_do: Finish the truck wrap and signage, create your Instagram and Google listings, and plan a daily posting routine for location and hours.
steps.tip: Check sign rules first so your signage is allowed.

steps.name: Run a soft launch
steps.what_to_do: Serve friends and family or a low-risk venue to test timing, menu flow, and food safety routines.
steps.tip: Time your average order. Speed matters more than most first-timers expect.

steps.name: Go live
steps.what_to_do: Confirm every permit is displayed in the truck and your first locations are approved, then open for business.
steps.tip: Alcohol and hiring can finish later if you launch without them.

steps.name: Set up your compliance routine
steps.what_to_do: Start daily commissary and temperature logs, calendar every renewal date, and schedule a yearly self-inspection.
steps.tip: Missed renewals are one of the most common reasons for suspension.

inspection_prep: Handwashing sink with hot water, soap, and paper towels
Calibrated food thermometers and temperature logs
Approved fire extinguisher with a current tag
Proof of commissary agreement on board
Copies of all permits ready to display in the truck
Approved menu and equipment list matching what is on the truck
Secured propane cylinders and working ventilation hood
Trash and recycling containers for customers
